notes:
Stage: procurement but effectively stalled / closed-lost to internal self-host. Short, choppy CRM notes below.
- Background: Tier-1 fintech platform (payments + risk). Heavy compliance. Preferred full control of model lifecycle and data plane.
- Use-case summary: primary = risk scoring + real-time fraud signal enrichment + internal support assistant for ops teams. Secondary = doc search for compliance docs. Target latency p95 < 250ms for online risk calls; throughput baseline target 200 req/s daytime. Cost sensitivity: high — target <60% of hosted unit cost at scale.
- Tech preference: infra team explicitly building on vLLM + TGI for orchestration; GPU inference runtime explored: TensorRT-LLM for quantized 16/8-bit kernels. Leaning toward Llama-family 34B quantized or homegrown distilled variants.
- Security: InfoSec insisted on customer-managed KMS/HSM, full audit logs, and NO external control plane for models. Request: air-gapped option or VPC-only with private control plane. Redwood offered Private deployment + KMS integration, but InfoSec rejected any external control plane access. Quote from Head of Infra (M. Rivera): "We cannot accept an external control plane touching keys or routing policies — compliance won't sign off."
- Procurement & org: internal champion (Lead ML Eng, Maya Gupta) left 2026-01-09. After departure momentum stalled. Procurement signaled a near-term budget freeze for third-party SaaS inference (Q4 spend re-prioritized).
- POC history: ran a 3-week throughput/latency POC in Nov-Dec 2025 comparing Redwood Dedicated vs internal vLLM setup. Redwood demo showed better SLA stability but internal infra beat cost-per-token at projected scale (est. 50M tokens/month).
- Security review: completed initial questionnaire 2025-11-20. InfoSec escalated on 2025-12-08 requesting private control plane and HSM proof-of-concept. Redwood provided design doc (drive:/pacifica/deal-space/security-answers-v3.docx) but final signoff never granted.
- Decision: technical + cost + control reasons -> PACIFICA initiated self-host road map. Infra notes reference commit to vLLM/TGI + TensorRT-LLM stack, multi-zone GPU clusters, private KMS.
- Competitive notes: Anthropic evaluated for hosted safety features but failed residency/KMS checks; OpenAI pilot showed good model quality but unacceptable from audit perspective. Ultimately decision: self-host.
- Quotes from CIO (S. Patel): "We need absolute control of keys and model artifacts. If that means extra infra ops, so be it."
- Next recommended Redwood approach: position Optimize for cost/quantization advising, and keep 'private hybrid' playbook ready (fallback routing + local cache) — ask to re-open if champion returns or budget frees.
- Current status: Account marked low-priority, monitoring for signals (re-org, budget re-open, new champion).
